GeneSummary.bullet_point: NIF3 is classified as one of the NIF-like phosphatases in the Plasmodium phosphatome and is part of a family where the common substrate is the C-terminal domain of RNA polymerase II.
GeneSummary.evidence_location: Results section - paragraph 1 and Discussion section
supporting_quotes: PFam domains were used to define protein sets with similarity to PPP, PTP, PPM, NIF-like, and PTP-like A families.
the inability to delete three FCPs (NIF2, NIF3, and NIF4) is not surprising, as the common substrate of FCPs is the C-terminal domain of RNA polymerase II

GeneSummary.bullet_point: NIF3 was refractory to deletion attempts, suggesting it is essential for parasite survival during asexual blood stage development.
supporting_quotes: A total of 178 individual gene deletion attempts were performed (at least 4 per gene; Table S1), resulting in successful deletion of 14 PPs (47%)
the inability to delete three FCPs (NIF2, NIF3, and NIF4) is not surprising

GeneSummary.bullet_point: NIF3 has conserved metal coordinating residues and phosphate-binding residues based on computational structural analysis using available experimental template structures.
supporting_quotes: computational structural analysis has further supported the presence and correct position of phosphate and metal-coordinating residues in all PPPs, NIFs, and PPMs

AdditionalInferences: As a NIF-like phosphatase targeting RNA polymerase II CTD, NIF3 likely plays a critical role in transcriptional regulation, which would explain why it cannot be deleted without compromising parasite viability
The essential nature of NIF3 suggests it may be a potential drug target, as it appears to be required for basic cellular functions in Plasmodium parasites
data.ShortSummary: NIF3 is an essential NIF-like phosphatase in Plasmodium that targets the C-terminal domain of RNA polymerase II and cannot be deleted, indicating its critical role in parasite survival.

data.short_summary: NIF3 is a putative essential NIF-like phosphatase that likely targets the C-terminal domain of RNA polymerase II and contains conserved metal coordinating and phosphate-binding residues critical for parasite survival during asexual blood stage development.
